source.title: United Kingdom Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS). 13: Relative efficacy of randomly allocated diet, sulphonylurea, insulin, or metformin in patients with newly diagnosed non-insulin dependent diabetes followed for three years.

study.design: multicenter randomized treatment-allocation clinical report, three-year biochemical efficacy/adherence/hypoglycemia; no blinding method stated

metformin.titration: weekly, to maximum tolerated, fasting glucose target<=6.0mmol/l
metformin.route: oral tablet implied by doses/tablet discussion, formulation/release not characterized
metformin.rescue: glibenclamide then insulin if glucose>=15mmol/l or symptoms persist

sulphonylureas.rescue: metformin up to850mg three times daily, then insulin

insulin.initial: ultralente beef Ultratard MC then human Ultratard HM, NovoNordisk
insulin.additions: soluble insulin2-3times daily if premeal/bed glucose>7.0mmol/l; other formulations allowed

study.diet: all dietary advice; diet-only rescue secondary drug allocation at glucose>=15mmol/l or symptoms

assays.glucose: clinic assay, monthly QA coefficient variation<4%

populations.eligibility: newly diagnosed non-insulin-dependent diabetes,age25-65,referred1977-1987,FPG>6mmol/l twice; after3month diet FPG6.1-14.9 without symptoms
populations.exclusions: recent myocardial infarction,current angina/heart failure,accelerated hypertension,proliferative/preproliferative retinopathy,creatinine>175umol/l,life-threatening illness including cancer,systemic-steroid illness,insulin-precluding occupation,language difficulties,ketonuria>3mmol/l

estimate.obeseMetforminVsDietWeight: not significantly different, exactP not reported
